title: Cosmos DB Overview
description: Understand what Azure Cosmos DB is, its globally distributed NoSQL capabilities, and how it differs from traditional databases.

data.text: Azure Cosmos DB is Microsoft's globally distributed, multi-model NoSQL database. It offers **turnkey global distribution**, **guaranteed low latency**, and **five well-defined consistency levels** — all at the click of a button. Unlike traditional databases, Cosmos DB stores data in JSON-like documents and replicates it across any number of Azure regions.

data.title: What Makes Cosmos DB Different
items: **Global distribution** — replicate data across 50+ Azure regions with a single API call.
**Guaranteed latency** — promise 10 ms reads and writes at the 99th percentile, regardless of region.
**Five consistency levels** — choose the right balance between consistency and performance.
**Elastic throughput** — scale throughput up or down in real time without re-provisioning servers.
**Multiple APIs** — SQL (Core), MongoDB, Cassandra, Gremlin, and Table.

data.title: Create a Cosmos DB Account with Azure CLI
data.content: Provision a SQL API Cosmos DB account with two regions
data.code:
az cosmosdb create \
  --name cosmos-demo \
  --resource-group rg-demo \
  --locations regionName=eastus failoverPriority=0 isZoneRedundant=false \
  --locations regionName=westus failoverPriority=1 isZoneRedundant=false \
  --default-consistency-level Session

terms.definition: The top-level namespace for a Cosmos DB deployment that holds databases, containers, and throughput settings.
A schema-agnostic collection of JSON items with a partition key, throughput, and indexing policy.
A guarantee about how fresh reads are relative to writes, from strong to eventual.
A normalized measure of throughput required for database operations like reads, writes, and queries.

data.title: Start with SQL API
data.text: The SQL (Core) API is the most common starting point for new applications. It uses familiar SQL-like syntax but operates on JSON documents, not relational tables.

data.title: Exercise: Create a Cosmos DB Account
data.description: Provision a Cosmos DB account and create your first container.
steps: Create a Cosmos DB account with the SQL API and two regions.
In the Data Explorer, create a database named 'AppData'.
Create a container named 'Products' with /categoryId as the partition key.
Note the primary connection string from the Keys blade.
data.expectedOutcome: A Cosmos DB account with a database and container ready for application data.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Cosmos DB is a globally distributed NoSQL database with multi-model support.
It guarantees single-digit-millisecond latency at the 99th percentile worldwide.
The SQL API is recommended for new applications.
Consistency, throughput, and regions are all configurable per account.
data.takeaway: Cosmos DB turns global distribution from a complex engineering problem into a configuration option.
